summary: The Colorado River Basin Water Security and Infrastructure Act aims to increase water supplies and expedite water, energy, and infrastructure projects in the Colorado River Basin. It establishes expedited environmental review and permitting processes for covered projects, creates a federal financial assistance program for water augmentation projects with a two-to-one federal-to-non-federal funding ratio, mandates the operation of the Yuma Desalting Plant and the development of seawater desalination in Mexico to meet treaty obligations, and authorizes major federal water infrastructure studies and construction programs.

affected_groups.effect: Eligible for federal water augmentation funding, project prioritization, infrastructure studies, and programs designed to increase reliable water supplies.
affected_groups.group: States of the Upper Division (Colorado, New Mexico, Utah, Wyoming) and Lower Division (Arizona, California, Nevada)

affected_groups.effect: Eligible to receive financial assistance under the water augmentation program and included in project consultations.
Subject to expedited federal permitting schedules and able to use existing non-federal studies to satisfy program requirements.
affected_groups.group: Project Sponsors (States, local governments, public utilities, private entities)

key_provisions: Exempts covered projects located in or benefiting Colorado River Basin States from the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 and establishes expedited 180-day permitting timelines for final agency actions.

Establishes a Colorado River Basin Water Augmentation Program administered by the Secretary of the Interior, providing $2 in federal financial assistance for every $1 of non-Federal funds, up to a maximum 66 and 2/3 percent federal share.
Creates a Colorado River Basin Water Augmentation Fund with an authorization of appropriations of $5,000,000,000 for the augmentation program.
Requires the Secretary to restore the Yuma Desalting Plant to operational status within 180 days, operate it at maximum technically feasible capacity, and authorizes $1,000,000,000 for the plant.

Directs the Secretary of State and other officials to negotiate with Mexico to develop seawater desalination facilities to offset United States obligations under the Mexican Water Treaty, supported by an authorization of $1,000,000,000.

Authorizes the Secretary to conduct feasibility studies and construct federal water infrastructure projects in California, Arizona, Nevada, and the Upper Basin states, backed by an authorization of appropriations of $12,000,000,000.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Colorado River Basin Water Security and Infrastructure Act aims to increase water supplies and expedite water, energy, and infrastructure projects in the Colorado River Basin. It establishes expedited environmental review and permitting processes for covered projects, creates a federal financial assistance program for water augmentation projects with a two-to-one federal-to-non-federal funding ratio, mandates the operation of the Yuma Desalting Plant and the development of seawater desalination in Mexico to meet treaty obligations, and authorizes major federal water infrastructure studies and construction programs.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation introduces substantial changes to water management, environmental review exemptions, and federal spending across the Colorado River Basin states. By authorizing billions of dollars in appropriations and exempting covered water and energy projects from the National Environmental Policy Act, the bill significantly alters the regulatory and financial landscape for western water infrastructure. Its score is 85 out of 100 for sweeping structural and funding changes.
